title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 86 of the Mg,ν notes opens §13, 'Digression(s) sur stratifications locales en général'. It follows directly from the previous page. There Grothendieck saw that gluing the Galois (locally constant) topoi of an open part X* and of a tubular 'boundary' D*∞ → D∞ does not recover the homotopy type of X (the case S² = C ∪ {∞}). That raised the general question of the homotopy type of a topos glued from an open set and its closed complement. To set this up, he defines a 'global stratification' of a topological space X as a partition (X_i)_{i∈I} into strata with these properties:
(a) the X_i are locally closed and the family is locally finite;
(b) each X_i is a manifold (variété);
(c) the strata are locally connected. If one wants connected strata, one assumes a frontier-type condition: for each connected component X_{i,α} of X_i and each j, the set closure(X_{i,α}) ∩ X_j is a union of connected components of X_j. Replacing the X_i by the X_{i,α} then preserves (a)-(c).
(d) a local connectedness ('unibranch') condition: for every X_i and every x in closure(X_i), the germ of X_i at x is connected. Two examples are excluded. The first is the stratification of a curve with a normal-crossing node (node plus its complement): near the node the 1-dimensional stratum has several local branches. The second is a closed disc with a marked boundary point (0-, 1- and 2-dimensional strata): near the point the 1-stratum has two branches.
(e), sharpened on the next page: along each X_i, the configuration of the closures of the X_j that contain X_i is locally a product X_i × Z. Here X_i corresponds to a point z0 lying in all the closures of the Z_j, and z0 has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods whose traces on each Z_j are connected. In modern terms this is local topological triviality along strata (Thom–Mather/Whitney style) plus connectedness of the local links of each stratum in every higher stratum.
The next page then observes the following. Global stratifications restrict to open sets (after taking connected components), giving a presheaf U ↦ Strat_glob(U). Because of the examples in (d), and of foliations, this presheaf is not a sheaf. Its sheafification defines 'local stratifications', which he compares with the SGA4 discussion of local equivalence relations.
The purpose in context: the Deligne–Mumford boundary of M̄g,ν is a normal-crossings divisor whose components self-intersect (e.g. Δ0). Its natural stratification by dual graphs is exactly of the excluded type (d), but is étale/orbifold-locally a 'good' stratification. A local notion is therefore needed to describe the 'structure at infinity' and the homotopy type glued from the strata's tubular neighbourhoods.
errors: Condition (c) 'loc. connexes' is redundant given (b): manifolds are automatically locally connected. The real content is the frontier condition on connected components.

Condition (d) as stated (connected germ of X_i at each x in its closure) must be read as 'there exists a fundamental system of neighbourhoods V of x with V∩X_i connected'. Grothendieck makes this precise only in (e) on the next page.
The definition is a sketch. No condition is imposed relating the dimensions of strata, and 'variété' is left unspecified (topological, presumably).

ideas.what: Definition of a global stratification with locally closed, locally finite manifold strata and a frontier condition on connected components
ideas.modern_name: Stratified space satisfying the frontier condition (Whitney/Thom–Mather style, topological)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (1950s–70s); Goresky–MacPherson for the topological version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses 'structures stratifiées' and tame topology, informally

ideas.what: Unibranch/local-connectedness condition on strata near points of their closures, with a local product structure X_i × Z and connected traces of the Z_j near z0
ideas.modern_name: Locally cone-like / conically stratified space with connected links; analogue of strict vs. non-strict normal crossings (unibranch strata closures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann (locally cone-like spaces, 1972), Quinn (homotopically stratified sets); the strict-normal-crossing distinction is standard in algebraic geometry

ideas.what: Global stratifications form a presheaf on X that is not a sheaf; its sheafification defines 'local stratifications', compared with SGA4 local equivalence relations
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications defined locally (étale/orbifold-locally), e.g. the normal-crossings boundary of M̄g,n; stacky/local versions of stratified structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on log structures and orbifold stratifications (Kato, Deligne–Mumford boundary analysis); not usually formulated this way

ideas.what: Motivation from the previous page: computing the homotopy type of a topos glued from an open set and its closed complement through tubular neighbourhoods of strata
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path ∞-categories and stratified homotopy types; constructible sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished 1990s), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the stratified 'structure at infinity' of Mg,ν and tame topology

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates a unibranch condition on stratifications and proposes 'local stratifications' as the sheafification of global ones. The motivating application is to non-unibranch stratifications such as the normal-crossings boundary of M̄g,ν (self-intersecting Δ0) and to the homotopy type of glued topoi. This anticipates the need, later met by exit-path categories with étale-local/stacky stratifications, to handle strata whose closures are not unibranch.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making the exit-path (stratified homotopy) type of the DM boundary work requires exactly such a local/stacky notion of stratification. The explicit 'sheafify the presheaf of stratifications' viewpoint is a clean formalism not commonly stated, though its substance is known to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: These are mostly standard stratification notions, sketched. Mildly notable: the explicit link to M̄g,ν's non-strict boundary and to topos gluing and homotopy type, and the definition of local stratifications by sheafifying a non-sheaf presheaf. Both anticipate later stratified-homotopy machinery but are not results.
transcription_corrections: Title is likely 'Digression(s) sur stratifications locales en général'. The comma after 'stratifications' is probably an artefact.

In (c), the marginal insertion reads roughly '(elles ne sont pas [nécessairement] connexes)'. The parenthesis '(sinon, on suppose de façon plus forte que b), que pour les composantes connexes X_{i,α} d'un X_i ...' is the alternative frontier condition.
In (b), the word after 'variété' is illegible. The machine reading 'de strates' is doubtful; the image suggests a crossed-out qualifier, probably 'topologique' or similar.
In (d), 'le germe d'espace des X_i en voisinage de x' is more likely 'au voisinage de x'.
